t.E353.agn: In 2020, assuming that the substance is completely broken down to tartaric acid before absorption, EFSA recommended that it be included in the group ADI of 240 mg/kg body weight per day set for tartaric acid–tartrates, and concluded that there was no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E353.body: Metatartaric acid is assumed to be completely broken down to L(+)-tartaric acid before being absorbed into the body.
t.E353.found.0: Wine and partially fermented grape must (only for tartaric stabilisation)
t.E353.found.1: Fruit wines and certain wine-based alcoholic drinks (in the EU up to 100 mg/l, limited to specific products)
t.E353.prod: Obtained by heating natural L(+)-tartaric acid above 150 °C (loss of water and esterification).
t.E353.regx.0: Re-evaluated; inclusion in the tartaric acid–tartrates group ADI (240 mg/kg body weight per day) was recommended; no safety concern at reported uses.
t.E353.regx.1: Permitted in oenological practices only for tartaric stabilisation.
t.E353.regx.2: 100 mg/l in fruit wines (14.2.4) and other alcoholic drinks (14.2.8), limited to specific products.
t.E353.summary: Obtained from tartaric acid. It prevents tartar crystals from precipitating in wine.
t.E353.what: Provides tartaric stabilisation by preventing tartrate crystals from precipitating in wine.
